title: Why Justin writes this defense
english: Romans, what happened yesterday and the day before in your city under Urbicus, and what rulers everywhere are doing in the same way without reason, has compelled me to compose this address on your behalf. You share our nature and are our brothers, even if you do not know it and do not wish it because of the prestige of what you consider honors.

For everywhere, whenever a person is being brought to self-control by a father or neighbor or child or friend or brother or husband or wife because of that person's deficiency, the wicked demons hate us and prepare to murder us. They have such judges as their subjects and servants, as rulers who are demon-possessed. This happens because of the difficulty of change, the love of pleasure, and the difficulty of moving toward the good. I am speaking apart from those who have been persuaded that the unjust and licentious will be punished in eternal fire, while the virtuous and those who have lived like Christ will be united with God in freedom from passion. By those I mean the people who have become Christians.
So that the cause of everything that happened under Urbicus may become clear to you, I will report what was done.
orientation: Justin is opening his Second Apology, addressing the Romans about recent unjust actions against Christians under Urbicus and elsewhere.

title: The case of the Christian woman, Ptolemy, Lucius, and a third Christian under Urbicus
english: A certain woman had lived with a husband who acted licentiously, and she herself had also acted licentiously before. But when she learned the teachings of Christ, she was made chaste, and she tried to persuade her husband likewise to be chaste, presenting the teachings to him and announcing the punishment that will come in eternal fire for those who do not live chastely and with right reason. He, however, continued in the same licentious acts and by his actions made his wife a stranger to him. For the woman now considered it impious to lie with a man who, contrary to the law of nature and contrary to justice, tried to make every path a path of pleasure, and she resolved to separate from the marriage.

When her own people entreated her to remain still, advising her in the hope that her husband would one day come to a change, she forced herself and remained. But when her husband went to Alexandria and was reported to be doing even worse things, she gave him what is called among you Romans a bill of divorce and separated, so that by remaining in the marriage and sharing his table and bed she might not become a partner in his injustices and impieties.

But this fine and noble husband of hers, when he ought to have rejoiced that she had stopped the acts she once did easily with servants and hired men, delighting in drunkenness and every vice, and that she wanted him also to stop doing the same things, when she departed against his will, he brought an accusation against her, saying that she was a Christian. And she submitted a petition to you, the emperor, asking first to be permitted to arrange her own affairs, and then to make her defense concerning the accusation after the arrangement of her affairs, and you granted this.

But her former husband, no longer able to speak against her at that time, turned against a certain Ptolemy, whom Urbicus had summoned, who had become her teacher in the Christian teachings, in this way. He persuaded a centurion, a friend of his, who had thrown Ptolemy into chains, to seize Ptolemy and ask him this one thing only: whether he was a Christian. And Ptolemy, being a man who loved truth and was not deceitful or false-speaking, confessed himself to be a Christian, and the centurion made him be put in chains and punished him in prison for a long time.

Finally, when the man was brought before Urbicus, he was examined in the same way on this one thing only: whether he was a Christian. And again, knowing the good things in himself through the teaching from Christ, he confessed that he was a Christian. For whoever denies anything either becomes a denier because he has condemned the matter, or because he knows himself unworthy and alien to the matter he flees confession; none of which belongs to the true Christian.

And when Urbicus ordered him to be led away, a certain Lucius, himself also being a Christian, seeing the judgment that had been made so irrationally, said to Urbicus: "What is the reason that you have punished this man, who has been convicted neither as an adulterer nor a fornicator nor a murderer nor a thief nor a robber nor simply as having done any wrong, but who confesses the name of Christian? Urbicus, you judge things not fitting for a pious emperor, nor for a philosopher son of Caesar, nor for the sacred senate."

And Urbicus, answering nothing else, also said to Lucius: "You seem to me to be such a one also." And when Lucius said: "Most certainly," Urbicus ordered him also to be led away. And Lucius confessed that he was grateful, knowing that he was delivered from such wicked masters and was going to the Father and King of the heavens. And another third man also came forward and was also sentenced to be punished.
orientation: Justin is reporting to the Roman Senate and people the events that happened under the urban prefect Urbicus, beginning with a Christian woman who separated from her unchaste husband.

title: Why Christians do not kill themselves and why they confess fearlessly
english: But someone may say, "All of you, then, kill yourselves and go now to God, and stop causing us trouble." I will explain why we do not do this, and why, when we are examined, we confess fearlessly.

We have been taught that God did not make the world in vain, but for the sake of the human race. We have also learned that he rejoices in those who imitate the things that belong to him, and is displeased with those who embrace what is base, whether in word or in deed.

If, then, we all kill ourselves, we will be responsible, as far as depends on us, for no one being born and taught in the divine teachings, or even for the human race ceasing to exist. And if we do this, we ourselves will be acting contrary to God's will.

And when we are examined, we do not deny, because we are conscious within ourselves of nothing base. Rather, we consider it impious not to speak the truth in all things, which we know is also pleasing to God. And we are now eager to free you from unjust prejudice.
orientation: Justin is addressing the Roman Senate and people, explaining Christian conduct after recounting the executions of Ptolemy, Lucius, and a third Christian.

title: Why God lets Christians suffer: the fallen angels and demons
english: But someone may also raise this objection: if we confess God as our helper, why, as we say, are we overpowered and punished by unjust men? I will dissolve this objection too.

God made the whole world. He subjected earthly things to human beings. He adorned the heavenly elements to bring about the growth of fruits and the changes of seasons, and he appointed a divine law for them. All of this he clearly made for the sake of human beings. He then handed over the care of human beings and of everything under heaven to angels, whom he appointed for this task.

But the angels transgressed this order. They were overcome by intercourse with women and begot children, and these are the ones called demons. And after that, they enslaved the human race to themselves. They did this partly through books of magic, partly through the fears and punishments they inflicted, and partly through teaching about sacrifices, incense, and libations. These were things the demons themselves came to need once they had been enslaved to the passions of their desires. Into human beings they sowed murders, wars, adulteries, excesses, and every kind of evil.

This is why the poets and mythologists, not knowing that it was the angels and the demons born from them who did these things against males and females, cities and nations, attributed the deeds they wrote about to God himself and to his sons, to the brothers of those sons, and to their children, such as the gods Poseidon and Pluto. For they called each one by whatever name each angel had given to himself and to his children.
orientation: Justin is answering an imagined objection that if God were truly the Christians' helper, they would not be overpowered and punished by unjust men.

title: The names of the Father and the Son
english: The Father of all has no name that anyone gave him, because he is unbegotten. For whoever is called by a name has someone older who gave him that name. But Father, God, Creator, Lord, and Master are not names; they are titles drawn from his good deeds and his works.

His Son is the only one properly called Son. He is the Word who existed before all created things, was with him, and was begotten when in the beginning God created and ordered all things through him. He is called Christ because God anointed him and through him ordered all things, and this name itself also contains an unknown meaning, just as the title God is not a name but an idea implanted in human nature about a reality that is hard to explain. Jesus, however, has the name and meaning of both a human being and a Savior.

For he also became a human being, as we said before, born according to the will of God the Father for the sake of those who believe in him and for the destruction of the demons. And now you can learn this from what happens before your eyes. Many of our people, the Christians, have exorcised in the name of Jesus Christ, who was crucified under Pontius Pilate, many demon-possessed people throughout the whole world and in your own city, people whom all the other exorcists, enchanters, and sorcerers had failed to heal. They have healed them and still heal them now, rendering powerless and driving out the demons that hold people captive.
orientation: Justin is explaining to the Roman Senate and people why the God Christians worship has no proper name, and what the titles Father, God, Creator, Lord, Master, Christ, and Jesus actually mean.

title: Why God delays the end: the seed of Christians
english: This is also why God continues to delay the destruction and dissolution of the whole world, so that the wicked angels, demons, and human beings may no longer exist. He delays because of the seed of the Christians, which he knows in nature to be the cause of this delay. For if this were not so, it would no longer be possible for you to do these things and to be driven by the wicked demons. Instead, the fire of judgment would have fallen and judged all things immediately, just as the flood earlier left no one except the one alone who is called Noah among us and Deucalion among you, from whom so many people have again been born, some wicked and some good.

For this is how we say the destruction by fire will happen, not, as the Stoics say, according to the principle of the change of all things into one another, a doctrine that has appeared most shameful. Nor do we say that human beings act or suffer what happens according to fate. Rather, each person does right or sins according to free will, and the good, such as Socrates and those like him, are persecuted and kept in chains according to the working of the wicked demons, while Sardanapalus and Epicurus and those like them seem to be happy in abundance and fame.

The Stoics did not understand this, and so they declared that all things happen according to the necessity of fate. But because God made both the race of angels and human beings with free will from the beginning, they will justly receive punishment in eternal fire for whatever wrongs they commit. For this is the nature of everything created: to be receptive of vice and virtue. For none of them would be praiseworthy if it did not also have the power to turn toward either one.

The people everywhere who have made laws and practiced philosophy according to right reason demonstrate this by urging people to do some things and to refrain from others. And the Stoic philosophers themselves, in their ethical teaching, honor the same things steadfastly, which shows that they do not succeed in their teaching about first principles and incorporeal things. For if they say that what happens to human beings happens according to fate, or that there is no God besides things that are always turning, changing, and dissolving into the same things, they will be shown to have grasped only corruptible things, and to hold that God himself comes to be in all wickedness through the parts and through the whole, or to say that there is neither wickedness nor virtue. And this is contrary to every sound thought, word, and mind.
orientation: Justin is explaining to the Roman Senate and people why God has not yet destroyed the world, despite the evil of demons and wicked people.

title: Demons hate those who live by the Word
english: We also know that those who followed Stoic teachings have been hated and killed. They became orderly in their ethical life, as did some of the poets, because of the seed of the Word implanted in every race of humanity. Heraclitus, as I mentioned in my earlier defense, and Musonius in our own time, and others we know.
For as I have indicated, the demons have always worked to make hated everyone who strives in any way to live according to the Word and to flee wickedness.

And it is no wonder that the demons, being refuted, work much more to make hated those who live not according to a part of the seed of the Word, but according to the knowledge and contemplation of the whole Word, which is Christ. They will receive the worthy punishment and penalty, being shut up in eternal fire.
For if they are already defeated by human beings through the name of Jesus Christ, that is proof of the punishment that is also going to come upon them and upon those who serve them in eternal fire.
For thus all the prophets proclaimed beforehand that it would happen, and Jesus our teacher taught it.
orientation: Justin is explaining to the Roman Senate why Christians are hated and persecuted, arguing that demons cause this hatred against all who live by reason.

title: Justin's challenge to Crescens
english: So I too expect to be plotted against by one of those I have named and nailed to a cross, or at least by Crescens, that lover of noise and show. For the man is not worthy to be called a philosopher, since he publicly testifies against us about things he does not understand, saying that Christians are atheists and impious, and he does this to win favor and pleasure from the many who have been deceived.

If he attacks us without having read the teachings of Christ, he is utterly wicked and far worse than ordinary people, who often guard themselves against discussing and bearing false witness about things they do not know. But if he has read them and did not grasp the greatness in them, or grasped it but acts this way so that he will not be suspected of being such a person, then he is far more ignoble and utterly wicked, being inferior to common irrational opinion and fear.

For I want you to know that I approached him and asked him certain questions of this kind, to learn from him and to prove that he truly knows nothing. And to show that I speak the truth, if the exchanges of our words have not been reported to you, I am ready to share in the questioning again even in your presence; and this too would be a work worthy of an emperor. But if my questions and his answers have become known to you, it is clear to you that he knows nothing of our teachings; or if he does know, but does not dare to speak because of his hearers, then, as I said before, he is shown to be not a philosopher but a lover of glory, since he does not even honor the Socratic saying, worthy of love as it is: "But no man is worthy of honor before the truth."
But it is impossible for a Cynic, who has set up indifference as his goal, to know the good except indifference.
orientation: Justin, the author, is speaking in his own voice, explaining why he expects to be plotted against and why he considers the Cynic philosopher Crescens a slanderer rather than a true philosopher.

title: Answering the charge that Christians teach only fear
english: Some who are considered philosophers say that what we teach is mere boasting and scare tactics: that the unjust are punished in eternal fire, and that we urge people to live virtuously out of fear rather than because it is good and pleasing. So that no one may say this, I will answer briefly. If this is not so, then either there is no God, or, if there is, he does not care about human beings, and virtue and vice are nothing, and, as I said before, lawgivers unjustly punish those who transgress the good things that have been ordained. But since those lawgivers are not unjust, nor is their Father, who teaches through the Word to do the same things as he does, those who agree with them are not unjust either.

But if someone puts forward the differing laws of human beings, saying that among some people certain things are considered good and certain things shameful, while among others the things that are shameful to the first are considered good, and the good things are considered shameful, let him also hear what is said about this. We know that the wicked angels established laws resembling their own wickedness, in which the people who became like them take pleasure. And the right Word, when he came, did not show all opinions and all teachings to be good, but showed some to be worthless and some to be good. So to such people I will say the same and similar things, and they will be said at greater length if there is need. But now I go back to the matter set before me.
orientation: Justin is answering the objection of those considered philosophers that Christians use mere boasts and scare-tactics about eternal fire, and he is about to return to his main argument.

title: Christ is the whole Word, greater than all human teaching
english: Our teachings, then, appear more majestic than every human teaching, because the whole Word, Christ who appeared for our sake, became body and word and soul. For whatever the philosophers and lawgivers ever spoke or discovered that was good, they worked out by a part of the Word through discovery and contemplation. But since they did not know everything of the Word, who is Christ, they often said things contrary to one another.

And those who lived before Christ, when they tried to examine and refute things by reason according to the human standard, were brought into courts as impious and meddlesome. Socrates, who was more vigorous than all of them in this, was accused of the same things as we are; for they said that he was introducing new demons and that he did not regard the gods the city recognized. But he cast out of the commonwealth the wicked demons and those who did the things the poets said, he taught people to reject Homer and the other poets, and he urged them to gain knowledge of the God who was unknown to them through the search of the Word, saying: "The father and maker of all is neither easy to find, nor safe to tell to all when found." These things our Christ accomplished by his own power.

For no one was persuaded by Socrates to die for this doctrine; but by Christ, who was known in part even by Socrates (for he was and is the Word who is in everyone, and who foretold through the prophets the things that were to happen, and through himself became subject to the same sufferings and taught these things), not only philosophers and scholars were persuaded, but also craftsmen and entirely uneducated people, and they despised glory and fear and death; since he is the power of the ineffable Father, and not of human reason.
orientation: Justin is addressing the Roman Senate and people, arguing that Christian teaching surpasses all human philosophy because Christ is the whole Word of God.

title: Vice imitates virtue's true goods
english: We would not be put to death, and neither unjust people nor demons would be stronger than we are, unless death were absolutely owed by every human being who is born. Therefore, as we pay this debt, we give thanks.
And indeed we think it is good and timely now to say that famous saying of Xenophon to Crescens and to those who are as foolish as he is.
Xenophon said that Heracles, walking along a certain crossroads, found virtue and vice appearing in the forms of women.

Vice, with her delicate clothing and a face made lovely and blooming by such adornment, was immediately charming to the eyes, and she said to Heracles that if he followed her, she would make him live always in pleasure and adorned with the most brilliant adornment, like the adornment around herself.
And virtue, with a squalid face and clothing, said: "But if you obey me, you will adorn yourself not with adornment or beauty that flows away and decays, but with eternal and beautiful adornments."
And we are persuaded that everyone who flees the things that seem beautiful and pursues the things considered harsh and irrational is destined for happiness.

For vice, to screen her deeds, clothes herself by imitating the incorruptible things that belong to virtue and are truly beautiful (for she has nothing incorruptible, nor can she produce anything), and she enslaves the earth-bound among humans, putting her own worthless things upon virtue.
But those who have understood the things that belong to what is truly beautiful are also incorruptible through virtue.

This is what every sensible person must suppose about Christians, about those who strive in virtue's contest, and about the people who did such things as the poets said about the so-called gods, drawing this inference from the fact that we despise even death, which is to be fled.
orientation: Justin is explaining why Christians do not fear death, arguing that death is a debt owed by every human, and he turns to Xenophon's story of Heracles at the crossroads to contrast vice and virtue.

title: Why Justin did not believe the slanders against Christians
english: I myself once delighted in the teachings of Plato. I used to hear Christians slandered, yet I saw that they were fearless before death and before everything else that people consider terrifying. I reasoned that it was impossible for them to be living in wickedness and love of pleasure. For what lover of pleasure, what intemperate person who thinks eating human flesh is a good thing, could welcome death and so be deprived of his own goods? Would he not try by every means to live this present life forever and to escape the notice of the rulers, rather than denounce himself as one about to be murdered?

The wicked demons have already brought this about through certain evil people. For by murdering some on a false accusation against us, they have dragged our household slaves, or children, or women into tortures, and through terrible torments they force them to confess those things that are told as myths, the very things which they themselves do openly. Since none of this has anything to do with us, we do not care, because we have the unbegotten and ineffable God as witness of both our thoughts and our actions.

For why would we not also confess these things publicly as good and demonstrate them as divine philosophy? Why would we not say that we celebrate the mysteries of Kronos in murdering people and in drenching ourselves in blood, as it is said, the same things done for the idol honored among you, on which not only the blood of irrational animals is sprinkled but also human blood, when the most distinguished and noble man among you pours out the blood of those who have been murdered? And why would we not say that we have become imitators of Zeus and the other gods in having sex with males and mingling with women without shame, citing Epicurus and the writings of the poets as our defense?

But since we persuade people to flee these teachings and those who have done and imitated such things, as we have also now contended through these words, we are attacked in many ways. But we do not care, since we know that God is the just overseer of all things.

If only someone would now climb up on a high platform and cry out with a tragic voice: "Be ashamed, be ashamed, you who attribute to the innocent the things you yourselves do openly, and who clothe them with the qualities that belong to you and to your gods, things in which they have no share at all, not even in the slightest degree. Change your ways; come to your senses."
orientation: Justin is speaking in his own voice, explaining how he himself once heard Christians slandered yet saw them fearless before death, and now he protests the slanders and persecution.

title: The seed of the Word and the whole Word
english: I too once learned that wicked demons had wrapped a slanderous covering around the divine teachings of Christians to turn other people away, and that they were spreading lies about these teachings. So I laughed at that covering and at the opinion held by the many.

I confess that I both pray and struggle with all my might to be found a Christian. Not because Plato's teachings are foreign to Christ's, but because they are not entirely like his, just as the teachings of the others are not either, whether Stoics, poets, or historians.

For each of them spoke well when he saw what is akin from a part of the seed of the divine Word. But those who have contradicted themselves in more important matters clearly did not possess unerring knowledge and irrefutable understanding.

Whatever has been said well by anyone belongs to us Christians. For after God we worship and love the Word who comes from the unbegotten and ineffable God, since he also became human for our sake, so that having become a partaker of our sufferings he might also bring healing.

For all the writers were able to see reality only dimly through the seed of the Word that was in them. For the seed of something and an imitation given according to one's capacity are one thing, and the very reality itself is another, from which the participation and imitation come by his grace.
orientation: Justin is speaking in his own voice, explaining why he became a Christian and how Christian teaching relates to Greek philosophy.

title: Request to publish the defense
english: We ask you, then, to endorse what seems right to you and publish this little book, so that others may also learn what we teach and be freed from false opinion and ignorance of what is good. These people become liable to punishment through their own fault, so that these things may be known to all people, because the ability to know good and shameful is part of human nature, and because they condemn us—whom they do not know to be guilty of the shameful acts they allege—and because they delight in gods who have done such things and still now demand the same from human beings. For by imposing death or imprisonment or some other such penalty on us, as though we did such things, they condemn themselves, needing no other judges.
orientation: Justin, having explained that Christians possess the whole truth through the Word, now asks the Roman authorities to publish his written defense so others may learn the truth and be freed from false opinion.

title: Closing appeal for publication and just judgment
english: I also despised the impious and deceitful teaching of the Simonians in my own nation. If you publish this, we will make it clear to everyone, so that they may change their mind if they can. It was for this reason alone that we composed these words.

Our teachings are not shameful by any sound judgment. They are superior to every human philosophy. Or if they are not, they are at least not like the teachings of Sotades, Philaenis, Archestratus, and Epicurus, and the other such poetic doctrines, which everyone is permitted to encounter, both spoken and written.

And now we will stop, having done as much as was in our power, and having prayed that all people everywhere may be deemed worthy of the truth. May you also judge what is just on your own behalf, in a manner worthy of piety and philosophy.
orientation: Justin is concluding his Second Apology to the Roman Senate and people, asking them to publish his defense and to judge rightly.
